title: Transplant status and rejection
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's transplant status or transplant complication only.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for heart-lung transplant maintenance.

HPI
The patient is a 67-year-old male who presents today for a routine follow-up regarding his status following a heart-lung transplant performed several years ago. He reports that he has been feeling well and maintains a stable functional status. He denies any shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant fatigue. He states that he is adhering to his current immunosuppression regimen and has not experienced any adverse side effects from his medications. He reports no signs of transplant complications and feels his current quality of life is excellent.

Medication List
- Tacrolimus
- Mycophenolate mofetil
- Prednisone
- Azathioprine

Review of Systems
The patient reports no constitutional symptoms such as fever or chills. He denies any respiratory distress, cough, or wheezing. He reports no episodes of palpitations or syncope. He denies any joint pain, rashes, or unusual bruising. He denies any gastrointestinal distress or changes in bowel habits.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives with his spouse. He enjoys gardening and walking. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Father had a history of hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on room air

Recent Labs
Tacrolimus level: 8.5 ng/mL
White blood cell count: 6.2 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL
Platelet count: 155 x 10^3/uL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He is in no acute distress. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Extremities are without edema. Skin is intact with no signs of new rashes or lesions.

Assessment
The patient is a 67-year-old male who is stable following his previous heart-lung transplant. He is currently tolerating his immunosuppressive medications well with no evidence of transplant issues.

Plan
1. Continue current immunosuppressive regimen as prescribed.
2. Routine monitoring of tacrolimus levels and renal function.
3. Follow up in 3 months for routine laboratory work and clinic visit.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Heart and lungs transplant status: one code, Z94.3, which maps to two HCCs (221 and 276).

distractors.why: Both heart and lungs were transplanted: Z94.3.
